title: kbid.py add keeps every row when parallel research agents add sources at once
goal: kbid.py add holds an exclusive lock over its read, insert and atomic write of a root's sources file, so concurrent adds from parallel research subagents neither drop a row nor leave a torn one; seen in the SP-wwacrsqr research story, where eight subagents adding sources at once left garbage rows at the end of the public root's sources file and dropped seven rows the worker had to rebuild by hand (SP-wwacrsqr retrospective).

clauses.clause: kbid.py add holds an exclusive lock over its read, insert and atomic write of a root's sources file, so concurrent adds from parallel research subagents neither drop a row nor leave a torn one

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 12 of 19, "Content fixes: answers, conflicts, gaps and source rows say what holds now"): a lookup returns a wrong or missing fact until it is fixed, which the held-out answer-rate fitness test of EP-gzr4mmkm reads. Premise run at plan time on the base: kbid.add_source (kbid.py:268-303) reads the csv, inserts and writes atomically with no lock, so two concurrent adds lose one insert; the check names a test that does not exist yet (exit 2). The test goes in _tools/test_redact.py, which holds the kbid tests; a new test id needs room under max_ids of _tools/tests_ceiling.json, else it replaces one, and the ceiling is never edited. A stdlib lock only: fcntl is not on win32, so use an exclusive-create lock file or msvcrt as kb/_self/code.md portability says.
